title: Chronicler game-system template
description: A character-sheet template: the properties a character has and how they are laid out. Authored as YAML or JSON on the Game System admin page.

system.description: The game system's name, e.g. "Monster of the Week". Shown as the template title.

version.description: Integer schema version for this system. Raise it when you change the shape of the template.

properties.description: The stats, tracks, notes and lists a character of this system has.

layout.description: Ordered sections grouping property ids for display. Any property left out falls into a trailing "Other" section.

rolls.description: The named things a character does — "Act Under Pressure", "Longsword" — each with the dice it rolls. Addressed by id from the Slack bot (/game roll).

effects.description: The temporary modifiers this system hands out — "+1 forward", "Queasy", "Taunted". A template declares only the vocabulary; a game master applies one to a character (/game effect add wolf forward) and it then prints as its own labeled, signed term in every roll it touches. Nothing expires by itself: the term showing up in a roll it no longer belongs in is how a stale effect gets caught.

functions.name: floor
functions.doc: Round down to the nearest whole number — e.g. `floor(7 / 2)` is 3. The usual choice for "round down" game math.

functions.name: ceil
functions.doc: Round up to the nearest whole number — e.g. `ceil(7 / 2)` is 4.

functions.name: round
functions.doc: Round to the nearest whole number — e.g. `round(2.5)` is 3.

functions.name: min
functions.doc: The smallest of the values — e.g. `min(harm["current"], 3)` never exceeds 3.

functions.name: max
functions.doc: The largest of the values — e.g. `max(strength, dexterity)`.

id.description: Stable machine id: lowercase, starts with a letter, letters/digits/underscore only. Referenced by layout and formulas. The word "entry" is reserved — formulas use entry["…"] to reach a list entry's own fields.

label.description: Human-readable name shown on the sheet.

type.description: What kind of value this property holds.
markdownEnumDescriptions: A whole number, optionally bounded by `min`/`max`. Negative ranges render signed (e.g. +2).
A running count from `start`, optionally capped by `max`.
Any subset of `options`, each checked on or off.
A repeatable list of entries, each with its own `fields`. Edited in wp-admin only.

One opinion set per player character — a 0..`length` rating track plus a notes box, labeled with the PC's name. Renders on NPC pages only. Each set is a personal notebook: visible and live-editable solely by its PC's own player, with GMs seeing every set.

A dice pool the character owns, as notation (`3d4`, `2d6+1d4`, `2d6kh1`). Rollable directly (/game roll gut) and spliceable into system rolls as a bare {id} placeholder. Validated leniently: an unparseable value saves fine and simply offers no roll.

live.description: Players may change this from the play surfaces (front-end / /sheet). Never combine with gm_only.

gm_only.description: Rendered only for a GM; omitted from the page entirely for players and the public.

owner_only.description: Rendered only for the character's author (the owning player) and GMs; omitted from the page entirely for fellow players and the public. Never combine with gm_only.

always_show.description: Keep the property on the sheet even when empty (e.g. Notes) instead of hiding a blank row.

detail.description: System-default note for what the property does (e.g. the moves a rating rolls). Characters may override it.

derived.description: A formula (Symfony Expression Language) computed on every read from other properties. Supported on number and toggle. Never stored or directly editable. Reference properties by bare id; track, counter and checklist parts use brackets, e.g. harm["current"] or moves["the_big_entrance"] (1 when checked, 0 when not). Functions: floor, ceil, round, min, max.

min.description: Lower bound for a number property.

max.description: Upper bound for a number or counter.

length.description: Number of boxes in a track.

options.description: Choices for a select or checklist.

fields.description: Per-entry fields for a list property.

entry_label.description: Singular noun for one list entry (e.g. "Item").

label_field.description: Which field names an entry of this list in roll menus (/game roll). Must be a text field. Optional: defaults to the list's first text field.

id.description: Machine id for this field within a list entry.

type.description: Value kind for this list field.
markdownEnumDescriptions: A multi-line text field (compact textarea inside an entry).
A whole number, optionally bounded by `min`/`max`.
An on/off flag. Other fields can appear only when it's on, via `when`.

Dice notation with `{…}` placeholders, e.g. `"2d6 + {sharp}"` — the entry then offers that roll in /game roll, named by its text field. Placeholders may also reach the entry's own fields as `entry["…"]`: `"1d8 + {entry["harm_rating"]}"` on a weapon adds that weapon's harm rating. Pair with `when:` on a sibling toggle so only a taken move contributes. Validated leniently: a string that doesn't parse contributes no roll and is otherwise inert, never an error — but a placeholder that can't be resolved fails loudly at roll time.

when.description: An expression (same language as `derived`) over this entry's other fields — the field shows only while it's true. A bare toggle id works: `when: is_weapon`.

id.description: Machine name for the section, used to address it (e.g. from the Slack bot). Optional: when absent it is derived from the heading — lowercased, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to "_" ("Moves & Gear" -> moves_gear). Give one explicitly when the heading can't produce a valid id, or when two headings would derive the same one.

properties.description: Property ids placed in this section, in order.

masthead.description: Render inside the header card instead of as a body section.

id.description: Machine id for this roll — the first thing /game roll matches a player's word against.

section.description: Optional free-text heading grouping this roll when the available rolls are listed. Rolls without one fall into a trailing "Other". Unlike a layout section it needs no id — nothing addresses it.

dice.description: Dice notation: terms joined by + and -. `NdM` rolls N dice of M sides; `NdMkhK` / `NdMklK` keeps the highest / lowest K (2d20kh1 is advantage, 4d6kh3 drops the lowest); a whole number is a constant; `{…}` holds a formula in the same language as `derived`, evaluated against this character and added as a number — e.g. "2d6 + {cool}" or "1d20 + {floor(dex / 2)}". At most 10 terms, 100 dice and 1000 sides per term.

detail.description: What the roll is for (e.g. "when you do something under fire"), shown with the result.

id.description: Machine id for this effect — what a game master types to apply or clear it (/game effect add wolf forward).

label.description: Human-readable name, e.g. "Forward". This is what rides the term inside a roll: `+1 (Forward)`.

detail.description: What the effect is for, shown where it is listed (e.g. "+1 to what you roll next; clear it once it lands").

modifier.description: What this effect contributes, in one of two forms. A whole number is the sugar: that much (times the instance's amount) on every roll `applies_to` names. A string is a formula in the same language as `derived`, evaluated per roll, which picks its own rolls: it reads `amount` (the instance's magnitude) and `roll` — `roll["id"]`, `roll["label"]`, `roll["section"]`, `roll["uses"]` (the property ids the dice reach, so `'rizz' in roll["uses"]` catches every roll with Rizz in it) and every trait any roll in this system declares. It must produce a number; 0 means the effect leaves this roll alone.

applies_to.description: One target word for a whole-number modifier, matched in order against the roll's id, its label, a trait of this roll that is on, and finally a property id (matching every roll whose dice reach it). Leave it out and the effect applies to every roll. Trait VALUES (save == "dexterity") need the formula form.

cap.description: How far this effect's stacked instances can add up before they stop: apply Taunted three times with `cap: -2` and the roll still only loses 2. Bounds the sum per effect, in the direction of its own sign.

traits.description: Author-defined attributes saying what this roll IS, so an effect can target a category: `traits: { save: dexterity, magic_resistible: true }`. Names are lowercase ids and must not be one of a roll's own names (id, label, section, dice, detail, uses, traits); values are text, whole numbers or true/false.
